ai.claude: Every AI assistant that renders code, previews or apps inside the chat now has a browser-sized attack surface. The practical rule for any office, including architecture firms sharing chats: treat a shared AI link like an email attachment from a stranger, and keep client data out of tools that render untrusted content.
ai.fact: Simon Willison highlights a write-up by Parameter Labs showing how ChatGPT's sandbox for HTML previews could be broken: a math-keyboard component inserted raw HTML from a message, and a YouTube embed endpoint let JavaScript slip past OpenAI's security policy. A crafted share link could then read private data from another signed-in user. OpenAI fixed the bug and paid a $5,000 bounty.

src.t: Simon Willison: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts

ai.title: How one share link could have taken over a ChatGPT account

austrian.claude: This is the Austrian case at its most balanced: sound money as insurance, capitalism as the engine. The weak spot is the 6 to 8% figure: money growth is not inflation one-for-one, and Swiss M3 has grown far less, so a CHF saver's maths differs from a euro saver's.
austrian.fact: In his October report the German Bitcoin writer behind BlingBling says the money supply grows by 6 to 8% a year, so whoever holds no scarce assets gets poorer, yet his own portfolio has become steadily more stock-heavy. He cites global poverty falling from about 60% in 1950 to about 10% today.

opinion.text: gold and Bitcoin remain building blocks against monetary expansion, but stocks are the best way to share in humanity's endless problem-solving, and only someone expecting collapse should hold nothing but gold and Bitcoin.

mainstream.claude: Schweizerhalle is a rare case where a disaster produced lasting, cross-border fixes that worked. The lesson for today's chemical and battery industries along the Rhine is that retention basins and reporting rules are cheap compared with the cleanup.
mainstream.fact: On 1 November 1986 a fire at a Sandoz chemical warehouse in Schweizerhalle near Basel sent tonnes of pesticides and mercury compounds, washed out with the firefighting water, into the Rhine, killing fish and eels for hundreds of kilometres downstream. swissinfo marks the anniversary of one of the worst environmental disasters in Swiss history; the accident led to the Seveso-style major-accident ordinance and the international Rhine Action Programme, after which salmon slowly returned.

src.t: swissinfo: Schweizerhalle chemical disaster remembered 40 years on

thread.text: Talks move to a third day in Doha; Khamenei puts forces on alert and Tehran says it is debating its nuclear-weapons ban.
thread.title: Iran war

top.claude: Both sides are building leverage for the week after the vote: Washington by keeping strikes on the table, Tehran by floating the nuclear question and the mines. The nuclear remark is the more serious signal, because once a ban is publicly in doubt it is hard to restore, whatever Doha produces.
top.fact: Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third straight day of talks with Qatari mediators on ending the eight-month US-Israeli war on Iran, after more than 12 hours of Iran–Qatar talks in Tehran on Friday that were coordinated with Washington. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Trump has not decided on new strikes and prefers a diplomatic outcome, and Trump has said there will be no new attacks before the 3 November vote. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered the armed forces on Saturday to be ready to answer any attack, and security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran is debating whether to drop its ban on nuclear weapons if fighting resumes, though no decision has been taken.

top.claude: Polls missed Trump voters in 2016 and 2020, so a 9-point lead is less safe than it looks. The bigger story may be the Senate: if Democrats win it, Trump's nominees and any war-powers vote get much harder.
top.fact: Yahoo News' polling roundup puts Democrats nearly 9 points ahead on the generic ballot; they need a net gain of three seats for the House and four for the Senate, where they lead in Maine, Michigan, Georgia and North Carolina and are close in Ohio and Kansas. Trump's net approval stands at about −22.6 in the Silver Bulletin average. On the campaign trail he has tied government help to the vote, telling Camp Lejeune victims there is no compensation money if Republicans lose and saying in Kansas he would not allow year-round E15 ethanol sales if Democrat Adam Hamilton wins, the AP reports.

opinion.text: tying federal help to votes is a losing strategy for the president.

top.claude: The deal shows the new model of Western support: Washington sells, Europe pays. The bottleneck is no longer money or political will but factory output, which is why Europe's own missile production matters more than any single approval.
top.fact: The State Department approved the sale of 500 PAC-3 Patriot missiles worth $2.1 billion, funded by Canada, Germany and Norway and by the EU's Ukraine Support Loan, with no US money involved; Lockheed Martin is the main contractor. President Zelensky warned that deliveries could take several years, since only about 600 Patriot missiles are produced each year. Russian strikes this week cut power to about 200,000 households in the Dnipro region and 80,000 around Kyiv.

src.t: BBC: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine

top.title: US approves $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, paid for by Europe and Canada
top.why: Air defence is Ukraine's scarcest resource as Russia hits the power grid before winter.

top.claude: That a Republican state government is resisting a Republican administration matters more than the case itself: it shows election officials are guarding the certification process regardless of party, which is reassuring for the days after Tuesday.
top.fact: Alaska's Republican-led state government asked a federal judge on Saturday to dismiss with prejudice a Justice Department suit, filed on 22 October, that seeks to stop certification of the Senate race if Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan loses. The department alleges that Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign helped recruit a retired teacher also named Dan Sullivan to confuse voters, which Peltola denies; the state called the demand to segregate ballots impossible. A ruling is expected before Tuesday.

top.claude: TraderTraitor was also behind the $1.5 billion Bybit theft last year, so Pyongyang has now taken close to $8 billion from two exchanges in under two years. With the money moving into Ether and decentralised exchanges, the next test is whether swap services cooperate fast enough to freeze more of it.
top.fact: The FBI said on Saturday that North Korea's TraderTraitor hacking unit was behind the theft of about $6.3 billion from Binance, the largest crypto theft on record, confirming what blockchain analysts TRM Labs found on Friday. The FBI, Secret Service and IRS investigators are tracking the funds, which were mostly converted into Ether. Binance said it has covered about 90% of the loss, expects to restore withdrawals by Sunday and will absorb the full impact for customers.
